transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there! Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous activities, lifting heavy objects, pilates, yoga, or swimming for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thank you. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful. If you have these symptoms, we may need to assess this further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that covers everything I wanted to know. Thank you so much for your help!
